title: Shows with characters like Elliot(Mr Robot), Carmy from(The Bear), etc?

commenti.body: you might like Shameless, I haven't personally seen it in years but it was a solid college show to watch with the hombres and/or gf. sometimes there are smart ways the characters get out of trouble but they're generally fuck ups. it was pretty well written for the time too iirc

Marry Byrd in Ozark is very much in a similar vein as Walter White, if you haven't seen that show. If you haven't continued with Better Call Saul after liking Breaking Bad, give that a go. In addition to Jimmy, his brother Chuck could almost fit this description. 

I'll also say Twin Peaks because it's interesting to see the exact opposite in some ways. Cooper is very smart, and the show gets very dark, but his optimism and infectious joy are really interesting contrasts. I realize the character is pretty much the opposite of what you asked for, but if you want a show with similar vibes and are curious to see a different character, Twin Peaks should be it.  

Tony Soprano is at the very least a very inspirational character for these more recent takes. I don't think he has quite the same "drive" as Walt or Carmy, nor an equivalent technical knowledge as either of them in their respected fields. But it's a good show and an interesting character that still fits some of the same vibes. 

Hannibal might also be up your alley. Will Graham is a dark genius, and so is his counterpart, Dr. Lector. It's a lot more sensual and sexual than anything else I've mentioned, I'll let you decide if that's a plus or not. 

I'll also throw in Barry. He's a little different characterization, but there at least seems to be overlap in fan bases. 

Hope that helps.

Have you not seen season 1 of True Detective? Rust is possibly the GOAT tortured poet/genius character.

Besides that I think the professor from Casa de Papel kinda fits this description (the show itself is pretty schlocky though), same with Sherlock from BBC Sherlock. Tommy from Peaky Blinders. Also not a man but Brenda from Six Feet Under, maybe Beth from Queen's Gambit too.

Also not a genius but if you like self destructive artists you owe it to yourself to try Bojack Horseman.
Twin Peaks is a masterpiece but possibly the least fitting answer to this question.
I literally admitted that. I said it would be different. So, correct, thanks for agreeing with me.
